The event's entry from the loader: banks out BASIC and starts round 1 with the last player.
The record of the last player: players times 32, less 32 below.
After a throw. In practice throws again; in competition the next player throws, from the last player to the first, then the next round; after the third round returns to the menu through the loader.

Starts a throw: resets the stack, blanks the screen, silences the three sound channels, clears $10 to $49 and the javelin's sprites, draws the flags, copies the colour map and the start screen, sets the colours, starts the interrupt and the sprites, writes the status line, plays the tune, and waits in a loop for the interrupt to do the rest.
Copies the colour map at $C800 into colour RAM, 25 rows.
Copies the start of the field map at $C000 into the first screen, 25 rows.
Copies rows 0 and 12 into the second screen.
Loops forever: the interrupt runs the event.
Waits for line $64, turns off the CIA's interrupts, turns on the raster interrupt at line $25 and points the KERNAL's interrupt vector at irq.

Selects the video bank at $4000, sets the sprites' colours and pointers on both screens, puts the thrower and the javelin at X $36 and Y $AA, the shadow at X $C3, makes the shadow and sprite 4 wide and the javelin multicolour, and turns all eight on.
Sets the screen shown and the charset from A: $40 for the stands' charset, $48 for the field's.
The raster interrupt, through the KERNAL: steps to the next of three slots, sets its line and calls this slot's handler, written into the operand at $7D08-$7D09.
The handler's address, low byte, written by irq.
The handler's address, high byte.
Each slot's handler, low byte: $7D1C, $7D5F and $88CD.
The handlers' high bytes.
Each slot's raster line: $25, $91 and $F0.
The slot after each.

Slot 0, line $25: sets the fine scroll, swaps the two screens when the view has moved a character, sets the stands' colours and charset, reads the stick and runs the state of the throw. Then draws the next column into the screen not shown.
Slot 1, line $91: selects the field's charset and colours, counts the frame, and scrolls.

Moves the fine scroll by scroll_due. When it passes a character, shifts colour RAM a column and asks for the screens to swap; while the swap waits, copies the shown screen into the other one a column on.
The low byte of each section's lower half in the field map: $C3E8 for the first, $C5F0 for the others.
The high bytes of the sections' lower halves.

Draws column 39 of the screen not shown from the map: rows 0 to 11 from the stands at $C000, rows 12 to 23 from the section's lower half, characters and colours. After 40 columns moves to the next section and draws the next four flags.

Writes four flags into the map's barrier, rows 10 and 11, ten columns apart: six characters each from the flag's number, coloured from flag_colours. Then sets the two characters of the section's markings at $C783 and $C797.
Copies X rows of a column from the map to the screen, with the colours from the map's colour half to colour RAM.
Copies each row's character from the map and its colour.

Copies the first screen into the second one column on.

The speed across the screen each release angle adds: 127 times the cosine of the angle, from 0 to 90 degrees in steps of 9.
The speed upward of each release angle: 127 times its sine.
Shows the thrower's frame X: copies its three sprites from $9000 into $5080, sets the pointers of his head and body, places his five sprites from his position, and draws the javelin.
The operands at $8337-$8338, $833D-$833E and $8343-$8344 are written above with the frame's three sprites.

Runs the throw's state: 0 waiting, 1 running, 2 throwing, 3 after the landing, through the operand at $83AF-$83B0.
The state's handler, low byte, written by run_state.
The state's handler, high byte.
Each state's handler, low byte: $83B9, $8429, $84B6 and $85F7.
The state handlers' high bytes.

State 0, before the run: every 20 frames shows the next of six standing frames. In practice after a throw any push of the stick turns TRY AGAIN between YES and NO. A fire button pressed: on NO back to the menu, on YES the status line again; otherwise stops the tune and starts the run.
YES and NO.

State 1, the run: each frame adds the speed times 4 and $18 to a fraction; what carries over is the steps, 0 to 3. The view scrolls a pixel each frame with a step and the runner moves on by the steps less one; every five steps the next running frame. Each new press of fire adds to the speed, up to 31. Left starts the throw. Each step adds 0.0625 m to the distance; at 16.50 m the runner has crossed the line, a FAULT.
Starts the throw: frame 20, state 2, and a frame delay that is shorter the faster the run.

State 2: the throwing frames, 20 to 42. Up to frame 27 the runner keeps moving, a step every two frames, a FAULT at 16.30 m. Each time the frame moves on, the angle rises by one while left is held, to 10 (90 degrees), and falls by one while right is. At frame 33 the javelin is let go; from there it flies.

The javelin's flight. Across: each 64 of the speed scrolls the view a pixel and adds 0.0625 m; the thrower moves back off the screen. Up and down: four frames of five each 64 of the rising speed moves it a pixel; every ten frames gravity takes from the speed, and at the top the javelin turns and falls faster. The tilt follows its speed. It lands when, falling and on the screen, it reaches the ground for its tilt.
Rising: up a pixel; off the top of the screen hides the javelin.
Adds 0.0625 m to the distance, in decimal.
State 3, after the landing: runs the crowd while it cheers; a fire button starts the next throw.
Lets the javelin go at the angle: gravity from 4 to 7 by the angle, the speed across from the run's speed and the angle, and the speed up from the angle.
The gravity of each angle.
Places the javelin by the thrower's frame or in flight, and draws its image for the tilt into sprites 6 and 7, reversed when it falls. Draws the shadow under it while it is low enough.
The bar of the shadow, one to eight pixels.
The shadow's X offset from the javelin at each downward tilt.
How far above the ground the javelin lands at each downward tilt.

The javelin has landed. A FAULT scores 0. Otherwise the distance less 16.50 m is the throw, shown in metres with two decimals; from 48 m the crowd cheers, louder at 64, 80 and 96 m. A throw better than the player's best goes into the record with its text. Then state 3, and the footstep sound.
Keeps the better of the throw and the record's score, high byte first.
Writes FAULT in the distance's place and marks the throw a fault.
FAULT.
Clears the status line, writes the player's name, then PRACTICE or TRY AGAIN? in practice, or the round: 1ST, 2ND or LAST THROW.
1ST, 2ND and LAST.
THROW.
TRY AGAIN? and PRACTICE, each ending with a zero.
Writes the 16 characters of the player's record at (A, Y).
The low byte of the record's address, written from record.
Clears the status line, white.
Slot 2, line $F0: the status line, unscrolled on black with the font. On certain frames of the run and the throw plays a footstep, then runs the music and the sound effects.
The thrower's frames that put a foot down: 6, 13, 24, 27 and 30.
Every 6 frames copies the next of three pictures of the crowd into the stands' characters at $4700.
The low byte of each of the crowd's pictures.
Their high bytes: $AA40, $AB40 and $AC40.
Reads both joysticks; returns the port where fire has just been pressed, 0 for port 2 and 1 for port 1, or $FF for none.
Carry set when the player's fire has just been pressed.
Reads the player's joystick each frame.
The crowd's cheer: filtered noise on voice 3 at the volume A gives, held 120 frames.
A footstep: filtered noise on voice 3, 4 frames, unless one is sounding.
The SID offset of each voice.

The filter routing set so far.
The sound effects' timers, each frame: for each voice ends its note when its hold time is up and silences it when its release time is (the same timers as Rowing's).
Each voice's control byte.
Voice 3's control byte.
Each voice's hold time.
Voice 3's hold time, which footstep checks.
Each voice's release time.

The music driver, called each frame: for a new tune reads which voices it uses and starts each at its notes. Then for each voice, when its note's time is up, reads the voice's next bytes: $FF ends it, $FE lo hi jumps, $FD n sets the length of the notes, a byte below $80 is a note (an index into the frequency table, $7F a rest) followed by how many times the set length it lasts, and $FC is followed by pairs of a SID register and its value, until a byte of $80 or more.
Two bytes inside music_step that nothing reads.
Each voice in turn, from the third: counts down its note, repeats the length as often as the note asked, then reads its next bytes. Each new note first sets the test bit, restarting the waveform.
Two bytes after music_step that nothing reads.
Points voice Y at its notes from the tune's header.
Moves the music pointer on and reads the byte there.
Clears the gate bit of voice X, ending its note.
The offset of each voice's variables and SID registers: 0, 7 and 14.
The SID frequency of each note, low byte then high byte.
The table read one byte on, for the high bytes of the frequencies.
Each frame: the music driver, then frees each channel whose voice has ended.
A channel whose voice's timer reads $FF has ended: its priority and sound become 0.

Plays sound A and the sounds chained after it, each on the channel with the lowest priority, if that priority is no higher than the sound's, and unless it is already playing; returns $FF when no channel is free enough.
The channel with the lowest priority, in X, and that priority.
Starts sound Y on channel X: notes its priority and number, takes the voice out of the filter and points the voice at the sound's notes.
Stops sound A and the sounds chained after it, putting sound 0 on their channels.
The bit of each voice, for the filter.
Each channel's priority.

The sound on the third channel.

Each sound's priority.
The sound chained after each, 0 for none: 1, 2 and 3 are the tune's three voices.

The low byte of each sound's notes: sound 0 the last byte of the frequency table, $FF, which ends it at once; 1 to 3 the tune; 4 to 10 point into the code, left from another event, and nothing plays them.
